definition: Procure means to obtain, especially with care or effort.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word procure. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know procure should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: For the school's new darkroom, Mr. Vann procured chemicals no supplier would ship to a private address.
Get is the plainest rung under procure — no effort implied, no story behind the getting at all.
Obtain stops short of procure — a shade more formal than get, but still silent about effort; procure means the getting took work.

Acquire means to come to possess, by whatever route — purchase, gift, plain luck. It cares only that the thing is now yours. Procure cares how: the word carries the legwork, letters written and favors banked before the thing finally lands. Acquiring is the outcome; procuring is the campaign.

To source something is to find where it can be got — the supplier, the seller, the grower nobody else knows. Sourcing only finds the door; obtaining and procuring both end with the thing in hand, and procure adds that the getting itself took patient work.

The request slip asked for a 1911 county atlas, out of print for a century.

The librarian did not shrug it into the interlibrary queue; she set out to procure the thing, writing to two estate auctioneers, leaving her card with a map dealer in the next state, and cultivating a retired surveyor's widow for most of a year.
When the atlas finally arrived — water-stained but whole — she set it on the counter like a landed fish.
Procure is the exact word for what she did, because procure means to obtain, especially with care or effort — the getting has a story.
Get and obtain report only that the thing arrived; buy names nothing but the paying.
Procure smells of legwork: letters written, favors banked, sources worked patiently until the thing is in hand.
Procure is the quartermaster's verb: it flags that the getting was a project — calls made, sources hunted, favors spent.
Obtain is the formal neutral; acquire cares only that possession arrived; get is the everyday floor.
Reach for procure when the difficulty of the getting is the story, which is why armies and props departments live by procurement.

Their captain, Priya, took it upon herself to procure one.

She wrote to nine surplus warehouses, traded a spare chassis to a rival team for a lead, and sat through a ninety-minute phone call with a retired engineer who remembered one last shelf in a Cleveland stockroom.
The part arrived in November, packed in newspaper, and worked on the first try.
Anyone can buy what a catalog offers, the coach told the rookies afterward.
The season was saved by the slower art of the hunt — asking, trading, and refusing to hang up.
